title: Newsom Signals Openness to Expanding Supreme Court, Takes Aim at 'Perverted' Electoral College
snippet: California Gov. Gavin Newsom intensified his critique of national political institutions, expressing willingness to consider court expansion while slamming the Electoral College system.
content:
California Governor Gavin Newsom has significantly escalated his rhetoric regarding foundational U.S. political institutions, signaling an openness to expanding the U.S. Supreme Court while sharply condemning the Electoral College system.

A Radical Shift on the High Court

In recent comments addressing national governance, the prominent Democratic leader indicated that structural changes to the nation's highest tribunal should remain under consideration. Newsom's willingness to entertain court expansion—frequently labeled court packing by critics—comes amid growing frustration among progressives over the conservative supermajority's landmark rulings in recent years.

Sharpening Attacks on National Elections

Beyond the judiciary, Newsom aimed his sharpest criticism at the mechanism used to elect American presidents. Describing the Electoral College system as "perverted," the governor argued that the framework routinely undermines popular democracy by giving disproportionate weight to lower-population states at the expense of millions of voters in larger states like California.

As national political tensions continue to rise ahead of key election cycles, Newsom's outspoken stance highlights an increasingly vocal push among prominent Democrats to challenge traditional constitutional norms and push for comprehensive electoral reforms.
